title: Completed four-cell row allows a wall across a north-facing doorway
body:
﻿## Reproduction

Complete the authored `cell-row-four` at (10,10). Its lower pair of cells has north-facing doors at the shared corridor. After the plan finishes, submit an ordinary full-square `wall-brick` at (11,18), the outside approach of the western lower cell. `PlaceBuildOrder` approves it, although the door remains registered at the north edge of (11,20) and the interior is zoned. The same approval occurs after saving and restoring the completed prison.

Focused runtime test before the fix: 2/2 variants red (fresh and restored), expected `failed/unbuildable`, received `approved`. The pending ledger protects its whole rectangle while building, but that reservation disappears on completion. Existing completed-door protection checks only a later *template* wall on the south side of a room, not an ordinary wall at a north-facing door.

## Expected

The completed row's outside approach remains clear. A wall on an unrelated nearby corridor square still passes. The rule survives Save/Load and is applied by the worker's authoritative command path.

This is a new orientation and completed-state case under #1586, distinct from the earlier pending south-facing doorway repairs.
